subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted /exec session defaults be allowed to override later operator tools.exec security/ask config for Discord and other external-channel sessions, and what migration or reset policy should handle existing stored fields?
rationale: The code, tests, and docs currently make /exec a persistent per-session contract, but the reported behavior can weaken later operator security changes, so automation should not choose the security boundary or compatibility tradeoff alone.

options.title: Make operator config a floor
options.body: Treat global/agent tools.exec security and ask as a non-bypassable floor for stored session defaults and add focused migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Preserve session defaults with recovery
options.body: Keep /exec persistence semantics but add an operator-visible reset/audit path that clears or reports stored exec overrides after config changes.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave /exec session state precedence as documented and update operator guidance to use tool policy or explicit session reset when hard enforcement is required.

recommendation.title: Make operator config a floor
recommendation.body: Treat global/agent tools.exec security and ask as a non-bypassable floor for stored session defaults and add focused migration/reset coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The original /exec session override commits and focused resolver tests are tied to this account, making it the clearest routing candidate for the policy decision.
